title: How Bruce Lee Worked
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant trace the life and career of martial artist and actor Bruce Lee. They cover his mixed ancestry (Dutch Jewish great-grandfather, British mistress, Cantonese opera star father), his birth in San Francisco and childhood in Hong Kong, his child acting and street fighting, his Wing Chun training and the fight with Wong Jack Man, his development of Jeet Kune Do, his teaching in the US and the Green Hornet role, his Hong Kong films (The Big Boss, Fist of Fury, Way of the Dragon, Enter the Dragon), the myths about his speed, his sudden death in 1973, the legacy of his son Brandon Lee, and their assessment of Tarantino's portrayal in Once Upon a Time in Hollywood. The episode ends with a listener mail segment from Noah in Scotland.
topics: Once Upon a Time in Hollywood

entities.name: Once Upon a Time in Hollywood

segments.title: Opening banter and Bruce Lee movie watching
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about martial arts, kung fu movies, and Ricky O, then introduce Bruce Lee as the topic and discuss his cultural impact on Asian heroes in Western film.

segments.title: Bruce Lee's ancestry and birth
segments.summary: They describe Lee's mixed lineage, including a Dutch Jewish great-grandfather who worked for the Dutch East India Company in Hong Kong, and his Cantonese opera star father. Lee was born in San Francisco in 1940 and his family moved back to Hong Kong.

segments.title: Childhood, The Kid, and early fights
segments.summary: Lee was a child actor starting around age ten in the film The Kid. He was small and weak as a child, and he gained a reputation as a street fighter in Hong Kong. He lost a fight at around fifteen to a Wing Chun practitioner and then entered that school.

segments.title: Wing Chun and the center line theory
segments.summary: The hosts explain Wing Chun's center line theory and stand-and-guard principles, and how they informed Lee's fast close-range striking.

segments.title: Trouble in Hong Kong and move to America
segments.summary: Lee's father did not let him sign a child acting contract. After a fight with the son of a triad member and police warnings, his father sent him to the United States with money and family contacts. He settled in Seattle, where he attended college, worked as a busboy, and taught martial arts.

segments.title: Opening martial arts schools and the Wong Jack Man fight
segments.summary: Lee married Linda and had children, and he opened martial arts schools open to people of all backgrounds. He fought Wong Jack Man, a fight with conflicting eyewitness accounts that ended at least in a draw, and that fight led him to develop Jeet Kune Do.
topics: Bruce Lee boxing and fencing influence

segments.title: Green Hornet, grappling, and Hollywood career
segments.summary: Lee's fighting style expanded with boxing and fencing elements. On the set of The Green Hornet, stuntman Judo Gene LaBelle threw him over a shoulder, which led Lee to train grappling. Lee then returned to Los Angeles, got a role on The Green Hornet, and made friends such as James Coburn and Steve McQueen.

segments.title: Tarantino's portrayal and Lee's public persona
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the Once Upon a Time in Hollywood fight scene and criticism from Lee's daughter, Shannon Lee. They also discuss Lee's public insults of traditional martial arts schools, Roman Polanski's suspicion about glasses, and Lee's fitness focus.
topics: Once Upon a Time in Hollywood

segments.title: Hong Kong films, box office success, and speed legends
segments.summary: Lee returned to Hong Kong and signed with Golden Harvest. The Big Boss broke box office records, followed by Fist of Fury, Way of the Dragon, and Enter the Dragon. The hosts discuss his speed, legends such as catching rice grains with chopsticks, and the exaggerated six-foot punch claims.

segments.title: Death of Bruce Lee and legacy
segments.summary: Lee died in 1973 at age 32, a month before Enter the Dragon was released in the United States. They discuss theories about his death, including medication reaction and heat stroke, and the death of his son Brandon Lee on the set of The Crow. They also discuss his cultural legacy, Game of Death, and Bruce Lee imitation films.

segments.title: Listener mail from Noah in Scotland
segments.summary: Noah from Scotland writes in for his annual update, sharing what he has learned from episodes, including space weather, and his interest in chemistry.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck thank listeners and give the email address for contact.
